questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: What year is generally given as the fall of the Western Roman Empire?
options: 410 CE
476 CE
questions.why: 476 CE is the date historians usually give for the fall of the Western Roman Empire, when the last emperor was deposed. The other dates mark different events (the sack of Rome, the Norman Conquest, and the fall of Constantinople).

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: In the feudal pyramid, who sits directly below the king?
options: Nobles/lords
Peasants
Knights
Merchants
questions.why: Nobles and lords held land directly from the king in exchange for loyalty and military support, placing them just below him. Knights and peasants sit lower in the pyramid, and merchants weren't part of the formal feudal hierarchy.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Which one is FALSE about the Crusades?
options: The First Crusade's stated goal was to reclaim Jerusalem for Christendom
Italian port cities like Venice and Genoa profited from transporting and supplying crusader armies
The Crusades permanently secured Christian control of the Holy Land
The Crusades increased contact and trade between medieval Europe and the Middle East
questions.answer: The Crusades permanently secured Christian control of the Holy Land
questions.why: This is FALSE — the crusader states eventually fell and Jerusalem returned to Muslim control. The other three statements are true: the goal was reclaiming Jerusalem, Italian ports profited hugely from transport and supply, and the Crusades did increase long-term trade and cultural contact. The misconception is judging the Crusades only by whether territory was permanently held, rather than their lasting effects.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: True or False: After Rome fell, Western Europe had no organised government of any kind until the Renaissance.
options: True
False
questions.why: False — feudalism filled the political gap, with kings, lords, and vassals creating a structured (if decentralised) system of land and loyalty. The Catholic Church also provided organisation and authority. The misconception is imagining a total power vacuum rather than a shift to a new, less centralised system.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: A student says peasants (serfs) owned their own land and could leave whenever they wished. What's wrong with this claim?
options: Peasants were tied to the lord's land and owed labour or produce in exchange for protection
Peasants actually ranked above knights in the feudal pyramid
Peasants owed military service instead of labour
Peasants were completely free and paid no dues to anyone
questions.answer: Peasants were tied to the lord's land and owed labour or produce in exchange for protection
questions.why: Peasants/serfs were bound to their lord's land, working it and giving up produce or labour in return for protection — they could not simply leave. The misconception is imagining peasants had the same freedom and land ownership as lords or knights.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Which one is FALSE about Romeo and Juliet's author and context?
options: William Shakespeare wrote Romeo and Juliet
The play is set in Verona, Italy
Shakespeare invented the entire story with no earlier sources
Shakespeare wrote during the late 16th century
questions.answer: Shakespeare invented the entire story with no earlier sources
questions.why: This is FALSE — Shakespeare based Romeo and Juliet on earlier stories, including Arthur Brooke's poem and Italian tales. The other statements are true: he wrote it, it's set in Verona, and he worked in the late 1500s. The misconception is assuming Shakespeare's plots were always wholly original.
